verses.sanskrit: न बुद्धिर्न मनो नाहं न चित्तं नेन्द्रियाणि च | न पञ्चप्राणसमूहो नान्नकोशस्तथात्मनि ||
verses.transliteration: na buddhirna mano nāhaṃ na cittaṃ nendriyāṇi ca | na pañcaprāṇasamūho nānnakośastathātmani ||
verses.translation: Not intellect, not mind, not ego, not memory, not the senses. Not the five pranas, not the food-body — such is the Self.
verses.hindi: बुद्धि नहीं, मन नहीं, अहंकार नहीं, चित्त नहीं, इन्द्रियाँ नहीं। पंचप्राण नहीं, अन्नकोश नहीं — ऐसा है आत्मा।
verses.commentary: The Tejobindu's method is systematic subtraction. Everything that can be objectified — named, observed, or experienced — is NOT the Self. The Self is that in which all these arise and subside. This method (neti-neti, from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad) is not nihilism but precision: by ruling out everything that is not the Self, what remains is Self-recognition — not as a new experience but as the prior ground of all experience.
verses.wordMeaning: The Tejobindu's method is systematic subtraction. Everything that can be objectified — named, observed, or experienced — is NOT the Self. verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मैव सर्वमिदं जगत् ब्रह्मैव परमं धनम् | ब्रह्मैव चिद्रूपेण तु सर्वं ब्रह्म मयं जगत् ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaiva sarvamidaṃ jagat brahmaiva paraṃ dhanam | brahmaiva cidrūpeṇa tu sarvaṃ brahma mayaṃ jagat ||
verses.translation: Brahman alone is this world, Brahman alone is the supreme wealth. Brahman in the form of consciousness — the entire world is Brahman, mine.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्म ही यह जगत है, ब्रह्म ही परम धन है। चित्त-रूप में ब्रह्म — सम्पूर्ण जगत ब्रह्म है, मेरा।
verses.commentary: The declaration that Brahman is everything. The world is not separate from Brahman; it is Brahman appearing in the form of consciousness.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration that Brahman is everything. The world is not separate from Brahman; it is Brahman appearing in the form of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो ब्रह्मणि लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo brahmaṇ līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into Brahman. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव ब्रह्म में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into the absolute. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into the absolute. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं ब्रह्म नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ brahma nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual Brahman — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत ब्रह्म — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of Brahman: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of Brahman: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं ब्रह्मैव सर्वं ब्रह्म मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ brahmaiva sarvaṃ brahma mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is Brahman alone, all is Brahman in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब ब्रह्म ही है, सब ब्रह्म मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यदा दृष्ट्वा दृश्यमेव दृष्टा शान्तिमाप्नुयात् | तदा तदा भवेत् तत्त्वमभिन्नं शाश्वतमच्युतम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā dṛṣṭvā dṛṣyameva dṛṣṭā śāntimāpnuyāt | tadā tadā bhavet tattvamabhinnaṃ śāśvatamacyutam ||
verses.translation: When one sees only the seer after seeing the seen, then one attains peace — that which is distinct from the mutable, eternal and immutable.
verses.hindi: जब दृश्य को देखने के बाद केवल द्रष्टा को देखा जाता है, तब शांति प्राप्त होती है — वह जो परिवर्तनीय से भिन्न, शाश्वत और अच्युत है।
verses.commentary: The shift from seeing objects to seeing the seer. When awareness rests in itself, peace arises. This is the immutable Self beyond all change.
verses.wordMeaning: The shift from seeing objects to seeing the seer. When awareness rests in itself, peace arises. This is the immutable Self beyond all change.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो ब्रह्म वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo brahma veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows Brahman in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो ब्रह्म को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 — The Jivanmukta — Free While Living

verses.sanskrit: सुखे दुःखे समो योगी लाभालाभे जयाजयौ | यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ||
verses.transliteration: sukhe duḥkhe samo yogī lābhālābhe jayājayau | yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā ||
verses.translation: The yogi is the same in pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat — like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker. This is held to be the analogy.
verses.hindi: योगी सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि, जय-पराजय में समभाव रखता है — जैसे वायुरहित स्थान में दीपक नहीं काँपता। यही उपमा कही गई है।
verses.commentary: The lamp in a windless place — one of the most beautiful images in all Upanishadic literature. The flame burns, gives light, and does its work — but it does not flicker at every passing breeze. This is not emotional blunting or indifference; it is equanimity. The Jivanmukta experiences everything, feels everything, but is not moved from the central flame of Self-awareness by the winds of circumstance. The flame is unshaken not because nothing touches it, but because its root is in something the wind cannot reach.
verses.wordMeaning: The lamp in a windless place — one of the most beautiful images in all Upanishadic literature. The flame burns, gives light, and does its work — but it does not flicker at every passing breeze. This is not emotional blunting or indifference; it is equanimity. The Jivanmukta experiences everything, feels everything, but is not moved from the central flame of Self-awareness by the winds of circumstance. The flame is unshaken not because nothing touches it, but because its root is in something the wind cannot reach.
